note: Documented + gap-filled Chain Insights graph query recipes. ISO GQL quantified paths and shortest selectors on USE topology are bounded per the resource policy. Merged into the corpus by generate-query-corpus.mjs; facts recipes drive the translator conformance + T0b baselines. A recipe marked admits: false documents a refusal and names the code it must get in expects_code; the corpus leaves it out. A recipe on the chain layer is one keyed lookup of the chain node (Transaction, Block, Address or Head). The chain recipes go into the corpus with the scope chain, so the server gates them with the gate of the chain layer. They are also read by tests/layer-routing.test.ts and listed in tests/fixtures/layer-routing.json.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address {address: "5CF6Ruq6u7DoF6TYxyaFzEuviWi7tjvJtz19XgPS2b7XDCFM"})-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) WHERE t.block_date = "2026-07-11" RETURN to.address AS to_address, t.tx_id AS tx_id, t.block_height AS block_height, t.amount_usd AS amount_usd, t.asset_symbol AS asset_symbol LIMIT 10
recipes.description: One address and one day, with the other endpoint left open. A facts read names an address pair with one day, or one transaction hash, so one address is no pair: refused with facts_pair_required.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address)-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) WHERE t.tx_id = "0x350065e1a55d7272de562706fdea5f48ae83cf10e468e56b2209f8cfbaaf1901" RETURN from.address AS from_address, to.address AS to_address, t.event_index AS event_index, t.edge_index AS edge_index, t.amount_usd AS amount_usd LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Bounded row-select of TRANSFER edges by tx_id equality on an EVM network, where tx_id is the 0x transaction hash: the server finds the transaction's day itself, so the read names no day. The same public fixture transaction as recipe_facts_transfer_06, with the USD amount projected.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address {address: "5CF6Ruq6u7DoF6TYxyaFzEuviWi7tjvJtz19XgPS2b7XDCFM"})-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) WHERE t.block_date = "2026-07-11" RETURN count(t) AS transfer_count, sum(t.amount_usd) AS total_amount_usd LIMIT 1
recipes.description: A count and a sum over TRANSFER edges for one address and one day, with the other endpoint left open. An aggregate takes the same rule as a row read: it names an address pair with one day, or one transaction hash. Refused with facts_pair_required.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address)-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) RETURN t.tx_id AS tx_id LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Unbounded TRANSFER row-select with only a LIMIT: no address pair and no transaction hash anchor the read, and a bare LIMIT bounds nothing. Refused with facts_no_anchor.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address)-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) RETURN count(t) AS transfer_count LIMIT 1
recipes.description: Unbounded TRANSFER aggregate: no address pair and no transaction hash anchor the read. Refused with facts_no_anchor.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address)-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) WHERE t.tx_id = "0x350065e1a55d7272de562706fdea5f48ae83cf10e468e56b2209f8cfbaaf1901" RETURN from.address AS from_address, to.address AS to_address, t.event_index AS event_index, t.edge_index AS edge_index, t.amount AS amount, t.asset_symbol AS asset_symbol LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Bounded row-select of TRANSFER edges by tx_id equality on an EVM network, where tx_id is the 0x transaction hash: the lookup is served from the indexed hash columns of the transfers table. Anchored on the Robinhood fixture day 2026-07-11 (block 6600000, six edges), so a live run must return rows.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address)-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address) WHERE t.block_date = "2026-07-11" AND t.block_timestamp >= 1783738500000 AND t.block_timestamp < 1783738560000 RETURN t.tx_id AS tx_id, t.block_height AS block_height, t.block_timestamp AS block_timestamp, from.address AS from_address, to.address AS to_address, t.amount AS amount, t.asset_symbol AS asset_symbol LIMIT 10
recipes.description: A time window with no address pair. The block_date bound names the day and the block_timestamp bounds (epoch milliseconds, 02:55:00 to 02:56:00 UTC) narrow it, but a day alone anchors nothing: a facts read names an address pair with one day, or one transaction hash. Refused with facts_pair_required. Name both addresses of the transfer to read the window.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (from:Address {address: "0x2459dedb3012d1e929edd17df26620120bdf11bf"})-[t:TRANSFER]->(to:Address {address: "0x220bbea2c59e2a1b0a71ffba694834e6822c0b52"}) WHERE t.block_date = "2026-07-11" RETURN to.address AS to_address, t.tx_id AS tx_id, t.block_height AS block_height, t.amount AS amount, t.asset_symbol AS asset_symbol LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Bounded row-select of TRANSFER edges for one address pair on one day on an EVM network: each address compiles to one id lookup, the block_date equality names the day, and the returned rows are rendered as addresses. The pair is a documented example: zero rows is healthy.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address) RETURN a.address AS address, a.labels AS labels, a.risk_score AS risk_score, a.risk_level AS risk_level, a.is_exchange AS is_exchange LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Live Address projection returning address, labels, risk_score, risk_level, is_exchange

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address)-[flow:FLOWS_TO]->(dst:Address) RETURN src.address AS from_address, dst.address AS to_address, flow.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, flow.tx_count AS tx_count, flow.first_seen_timestamp AS first_seen_timestamp, flow.last_seen_timestamp AS last_seen_timestamp LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Live FLOWS_TO edge sample with from/to identity, amount_usd_sum, tx_count, first/last seen timestamps

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[flow:FLOWS_TO]->(dst:Address) WHERE NOT src:Pool RETURN dst.address AS to_address, flow.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, flow.tx_count AS tx_count, flow.first_seen_timestamp AS first_seen_timestamp, flow.last_seen_timestamp AS last_seen_timestamp ORDER BY flow.amount_usd_sum DESC LIMIT 50
recipes.description: Top live outflows from one address ordered by amount_usd_sum descending. The start guard NOT src:Pool keeps the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): a walk never starts at a :Pool, so a pool never lists the traders it paid.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address)-[flow:FLOWS_TO]->(dst:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"}) WHERE NOT dst:Pool RETURN src.address AS from_address, flow.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, flow.tx_count AS tx_count, flow.first_seen_timestamp AS first_seen_timestamp, flow.last_seen_timestamp AS last_seen_timestamp ORDER BY flow.amount_usd_sum DESC LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Top live inflows to one address ordered by amount_usd_sum descending, with the first and last seen time of each link. recipe_topology_05 reads the outflows. The guard NOT dst:Pool keeps the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): a walk never starts at a :Pool.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address)-[flow:FLOWS_TO]->(dst:Address) RETURN src.address AS from_address, dst.address AS to_address, CASE WHEN flow.amount_usd_sum IS NULL THEN "unknown" WHEN flow.amount_usd_sum >= 100000 THEN "large" WHEN flow.amount_usd_sum >= 10000 THEN "medium" ELSE "small" END AS amount_bucket, flow.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Bucket live flow edges into unknown/large/medium/small by USD amount via CASE

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[r1:FLOWS_TO]->(dst:Address {address: "5FHneW46xGXgs5mUiveU4sbTyGBzmstUspZC92UhjJM694ty"}) WHERE NOT src:Pool RETURN src.address AS from_address, dst.address AS to_address, 1 AS hops, r1.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, r1.tx_count AS tx_count LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Direct one-hop FLOWS_TO edge between two named identities (graph_query_batch hop_1). The start guard NOT src:Pool keeps the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): a walk never starts at a :Pool.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[r1:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]->(mid:Address)-[r2:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]->(dst:Address) WHERE NOT src:Pool AND NOT src:Protocol AND NOT src:System AND NOT src.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND NOT mid:Pool AND NOT mid:Protocol AND NOT mid:System AND NOT mid.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND mid.is_exchange IS NULL RETURN src.address AS from_address, mid.address AS mid_address, dst.address AS to_address, 2 AS hops, type(r1) AS first_edge, type(r2) AS second_edge, coalesce(r1.amount_usd_sum, r1.bought_usd) AS first_amount_usd, coalesce(r2.amount_usd_sum, r2.bought_usd) AS second_amount_usd LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Fixed two-hop trace from a source over FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED, skipping exchange and pool intermediates (graph_query_batch hop_2). It follows the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): the pool guards NOT src:Pool and NOT mid:Pool mean the walk never starts at or passes through a :Pool, so it never leaves one on FLOWS_TO, so it cannot fan out to every trader the pool paid, and SWAPPED carries the trace across a swap from payer to recipient. A SWAPPED hop reports bought_usd, the value the recipient received. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address) RETURN count(a) AS count LIMIT 1
recipes.description: Count of Address nodes in the topology graph

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH SHORTEST 1 (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"} WHERE NOT a:Pool AND NOT a:Protocol AND NOT a:System AND NOT a.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]) (()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(via:Address) WHERE NOT via:Pool AND NOT via:Protocol AND NOT via:System AND NOT via.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]){0,4} ()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(b:Address) RETURN b.address LIMIT 50
recipes.description: ISO GQL open target: the addresses the shortest FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED walk (1-5 hops) reaches from one anchored address, the guarded open-target shape of the chain-insights-cypher skill with a literal address. WHERE NOT a:Pool on the start and WHERE NOT via:Pool inside the quantified path pattern keep the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): the walk never starts at or passes through a :Pool, and only the address it reaches may be one. SWAPPED carries the walk across a swap. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH p = SHORTEST 1 (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"} WHERE NOT a:Pool AND NOT a:Protocol AND NOT a:System AND NOT a.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]) (()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(via:Address) WHERE NOT via:Pool AND NOT via:Protocol AND NOT via:System AND NOT via.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]){0,4} ()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(b:Address {address: "5FHneW46xGXgs5mUiveU4sbTyGBzmstUspZC92UhjJM694ty"}) RETURN p LIMIT 5
recipes.description: ISO GQL shortest FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED path between two anchored addresses, in the guarded route shape. The start carries WHERE NOT a:Pool and the quantified path pattern carries WHERE NOT via:Pool, so the route never starts at or passes through a :Pool; only its target end may be one. Both guards sit inside the path pattern, so the selector picks among routes that obey the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule), and SWAPPED carries a route across a swap; a WHERE after the pattern would run after the selection and drop the route instead. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH p = ANY SHORTEST (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"} WHERE NOT a:Pool AND NOT a:Protocol AND NOT a:System AND NOT a.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]) (()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(via:Address) WHERE NOT via:Pool AND NOT via:Protocol AND NOT via:System AND NOT via.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"]){0,4} ()-[:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(b:Address {address: "5FHneW46xGXgs5mUiveU4sbTyGBzmstUspZC92UhjJM694ty"}) RETURN p LIMIT 5
recipes.description: ISO GQL one-of-the-shortest FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED paths between two anchored addresses, in the guarded route shape. The start carries WHERE NOT a:Pool and the quantified path pattern carries WHERE NOT via:Pool, so the route never starts at or passes through a :Pool; only its target end may be one. Both guards sit inside the path pattern, so the selector picks among routes that obey the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule), and SWAPPED carries a route across a swap; a WHERE after the pattern would run after the selection and drop the route instead. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[l:LINKED]-(b:Address) RETURN b.address AS linked_address, b.network AS linked_network, l.basis AS basis, l.confidence AS confidence, l.source_event AS source_event, l.declared_owner AS declared_owner LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Live LINKED ownership-overlay probe for the fixture Address, projecting basis/confidence/source_event/declared_owner provenance

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[l:LINKED]-(owned:Address)-[r:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]-(b:Address) WHERE NOT a:Pool AND NOT a:Protocol AND NOT a:System AND NOT a.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND NOT owned:Pool AND NOT owned:Protocol AND NOT owned:System AND NOT owned.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND owned.address <> b.address AND a.address <> b.address RETURN a.address AS subject_address, owned.address AS linked_via_address, b.address AS counterparty_address, type(r) AS edge, coalesce(r.amount_usd_sum, r.bought_usd) AS amount_usd_sum, coalesce(r.tx_count, r.swap_count) AS tx_count LIMIT 25
recipes.description: AC11: FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED reachability UNIONed over one LINKED hop — actor-level exposure surfaced through an ownership-linked address, not only the subject's own edges. The pool guards NOT a:Pool AND NOT owned:Pool keep the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): the walk never starts at a :Pool, the money hop never leaves one on FLOWS_TO, and SWAPPED counts a swap counterparty. A SWAPPED hop reports bought_usd and swap_count. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "5GrwvaEF5zXb26Fz9rcQpDWS57CtERHpNehXCPcNoHGKutQY"})-[l:LINKED]-(b:Address) WHERE a.network <> b.network RETURN a.address AS address, a.network AS network, b.address AS linked_address, b.network AS linked_network, l.basis AS basis, l.confidence AS confidence LIMIT 25
recipes.description: AC5: cross-space LINKED probe — the only edge bridging the bittensor and bittensor_evm address-grain networks

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (owner:Address)-[operation:OPERATED_BY]->(operator:Address {address: "0xdd509c9f91f66a18802ef5b3d54c73b62ea1ca08"}) RETURN owner.address AS owner_address, operation.tx_count AS tx_count, operation.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, coalesce(operation.token_standard, "mixed") AS token_standard, operation.last_seen_timestamp AS last_seen_timestamp ORDER BY operation.tx_count DESC LIMIT 10
recipes.description: Canonical point-anchored OPERATED_BY probe (chain-insights#257): given one operator address, its top owners by mediated transfer count. Topology-only edge; anchored to a live high-fan-in operator verified 2026-09-01; zero rows is healthy.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (victim:Address {address: "0x1874a43d7c6d888f9eda3d22a3a49704e3cadb24"})-[paid:FLOWS_TO]->(pool:Pool)-[removal:REMOVED_LIQUIDITY]->(receiver:Address) WHERE NOT victim:Pool AND NOT victim:Protocol AND NOT victim:System AND NOT victim.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND receiver.address <> victim.address RETURN pool.address AS pool_address, receiver.address AS receiver_address, max(paid.amount_usd_sum) AS paid_in_usd, sum(removal.usd) AS removed_usd, max(removal.receiver_added_usd) AS receiver_added_usd, sum(removal.usd) - max(removal.receiver_added_usd) AS receiver_profit_usd, max(removal.receiver_provided) AS receiver_provided ORDER BY removed_usd DESC LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Rug pull under the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule): from a victim that is not itself a :Pool (NOT victim:Pool: a walk never starts at a pool), enter a :Pool on FLOWS_TO and leave it only on REMOVED_LIQUIDITY, to the address the liquidity was paid to. receiver_profit_usd is usd minus receiver_added_usd; receiver_provided true with a large profit is the creator's rug pull, false is a drain by a stranger. The victim's own removals are excluded. Zero rows is healthy: no pool the victim paid into has paid liquidity out. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (src:Address {address: "0x1874a43d7c6d888f9eda3d22a3a49704e3cadb24"})-[r1:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]->(mid:Address)-[r2:FLOWS_TO|SWAPPED]->(dst:Address) WHERE NOT src:Pool AND NOT src:Protocol AND NOT src:System AND NOT src.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND NOT mid:Pool AND NOT mid:Protocol AND NOT mid:System AND NOT mid.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND mid.is_exchange IS NULL AND dst.address <> src.address RETURN mid.address AS via_address, type(r2) AS exit_edge, dst.address AS to_address, coalesce(r2.amount_usd_sum, r2.bought_usd) AS exit_usd LIMIT 25 UNION MATCH (src:Address {address: "0x1874a43d7c6d888f9eda3d22a3a49704e3cadb24"})-[r1:FLOWS_TO|ADDED_LIQUIDITY]->(mid:Pool)-[r2:REMOVED_LIQUIDITY]->(dst:Address) WHERE NOT src:Pool AND NOT src:Protocol AND NOT src:System AND NOT src.address IN ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000", "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead"] AND dst.address <> src.address RETURN mid.address AS via_address, type(r2) AS exit_edge, dst.address AS to_address, r2.usd AS exit_usd LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Two-hop trace that never fans out through a pool, under the pool trace rule (skills/chain-insights-cypher, Pool trace rule). The first branch walks FLOWS_TO and SWAPPED through ordinary, non-exchange intermediates and never starts from or passes a :Pool. The second branch starts from an address that is not a :Pool, enters a :Pool on FLOWS_TO or ADDED_LIQUIDITY and leaves it only on REMOVED_LIQUIDITY. No branch leaves a pool on FLOWS_TO, so the other traders a pool paid on their swaps are never reached. The system guard NOT x:Protocol AND NOT x:System AND NOT x.address IN [the zero and the dead address] on the start and on every address in the middle keeps the walk off a protocol contract (a PoolManager) and the mint and burn addresses, which link millions of unrelated wallets.

recipes.query: USE chain MATCH (t:Transaction {tx_id: "0x350065e1a55d7272de562706fdea5f48ae83cf10e468e56b2209f8cfbaaf1901"}) RETURN t.status, t.block_height, t.block_date
recipes.description: One transaction by its tx_id: did it succeed, in which block and on which UTC day. The day is the key to name in a facts read of the transfers it caused. The same public fixture transaction as the facts recipes.

recipes.query: USE chain MATCH (b:Block {block_height: 79841521}) RETURN b.block_hash, b.block_date
recipes.description: One block by its block_height: its block_hash and the UTC day it belongs to. The block_date is the day to name in a facts read.

recipes.query: USE chain MATCH (h:Head) RETURN h.block_height, h.age_seconds, h.warehouse_blocks_behind, h.graph_blocks_behind
recipes.description: The chain head, and how far the warehouse and the graph are behind it. Head takes no key.

recipes.query: USE chain MATCH (a:Address {address: "0x2459dedb3012d1e929edd17df26620120bdf11bf"}) RETURN a.balance, a.nonce, a.is_contract
recipes.description: One address at the newest block: its balance, its nonce and whether it is a contract. Add at_block to read a past block, at least chain_admission.at_block_min_depth blocks below the tip. A kind is read from is_contract and nonce, never asked as a lookup label. The same public fixture address as the facts recipes.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Mixer) RETURN a.address AS address, labels(a) AS node_labels, a.labels AS labels LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Every mixer contract the registry loaded, asked by its mark. :Mixer is a node label beside :Address, so a label match is a probe the server admits and answers from the label index in milliseconds (9 Hearsay contracts on robinhood). Never ask with a text match over a.labels and no address: that scans every address and times out.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (p:Pool:Launchpad) RETURN p.address AS address, labels(p) AS node_labels, p.labels AS labels LIMIT 25
recipes.description: Virtuals launchpad pools, asked by two marks at once: :Pool from the DEX indexer and :Launchpad from the Virtuals labeler. A starting pool is :Pool from the day it is discovered, traded or not. Its labels name the agent and its stage, virtuals:<NAME>:bonding or :graduated.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "0x966890d38bfd587c9d6fd6123389dfe18ac9de0e"}) RETURN a.address AS address, a.token_standard AS token_standard, labels(a) AS node_labels, a.labels AS labels LIMIT 1
recipes.description: What one contract is: the BIBEL agent token carries :Token with token_standard ERC20 and :Launchpad from the Virtuals labeler. Say it is an ERC-20 token; never print the column name token_standard in the answer.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "0x02d9876a21af7545f8632c3af76ec90b5ad4b66d"}) WHERE a:NFT RETURN a.address AS address, a.token_standard AS token_standard, labels(a) AS node_labels LIMIT 1
recipes.description: An NFT collection is :Token and :NFT both: :NFT is the token contract whose token_standard is ERC721 or ERC1155. WHERE a:NFT tests the mark beside the anchor; an ERC20 would return no row here.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (p:Address {address: "0x00aea4ccd2a12f955bfae8b8741cbee14d38e755"}) WHERE p:Pool RETURN p.address AS address, labels(p) AS node_labels, p.labels AS labels LIMIT 1
recipes.description: Is this address a pool: the HOODRAT starting pool is :Pool although nobody may have swapped in it, because :Pool means a pool contract the DEX indexer knows, traded or not. An empty labels list beside the :Pool mark does not make it unlabelled.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address) WHERE a.address IN ["0x966890d38bfd587c9d6fd6123389dfe18ac9de0e", "0x09e9df72f639875b58dbfd356e31c47b0b87f65b"] RETURN a.address AS address, labels(a) AS node_labels, a.labels AS labels, a.token_standard AS token_standard LIMIT 2
recipes.description: A Virtuals agent is two contracts: the agent token (:Token:Launchpad, ERC20) and its starting pool (:Pool:Launchpad). Both carry the same named label virtuals:<NAME>:<stage>. A list of at most 25 addresses is an anchor.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (f:Address {address: "0xc63d7338c178e805c544b8f897066bd3bbcbe136"})-[:DEPLOYED_CONTRACT]->(p:Pool) WHERE p.total_volume_usd IS NOT NULL RETURN f.address AS from_address, p.address AS to_address, p.labels AS to_labels, p.total_volume_usd AS total_volume_usd, p.tx_total_count AS tx_total_count ORDER BY p.total_volume_usd DESC LIMIT 10
recipes.description: The pools of an exchange by one factory (skill chain-insights-dex, reference R3, and the pool read of meta_dex_lookup): the :Pool contracts the Aero concentrated-liquidity factory deployed, ranked by lifetime volume. Anchored on the factory, so it is admitted on any lane and answers in under 100 ms, however far behind the exchange family is; the factory comes from registry/robinhood.json.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (a:Address {address: "0x72e46c9edf828002fdbfdd0952419790576c0f18"}) RETURN a.address AS address, labels(a) AS node_labels, a.labels AS labels, a.is_contract AS is_contract LIMIT 1
recipes.description: One registry contract read by its address (the contract read of meta_dex_lookup): the Aero router is confirmed when the graph shows it as a contract. One member per factory, manager and router of the exchange, in one batch with Head and the pools read.

recipes.query: USE topology MATCH (s:Address)-[f:FLOWS_TO]->(p:Address {address: "0x7615926023bb149f36095645c2a81dc367d39750"}) WHERE NOT s:Pool AND NOT s:Protocol AND NOT s:System RETURN s.address AS from_address, p.address AS to_address, f.amount_usd_sum AS amount_usd_sum, f.tx_count AS tx_count, f.last_seen_timestamp AS last_seen_timestamp, s.is_contract AS from_is_contract ORDER BY f.amount_usd_sum DESC LIMIT 25
recipes.description: The sellers into one pool (skills chain-insights-dex and chain-insights-dex-gauge, reference G1): the senders on FLOWS_TO into the busiest Aero pool, ranked by lifetime volume. The biggest are often contracts and liquidity managers, which the skill names as such.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (s:Address {address: "0x4b9364c8553c519a419b259f022865071fd7bfdf"})-[x:SWAP]->(r:Address {address: "0x72e46c9edf828002fdbfdd0952419790576c0f18"}) WHERE x.block_date = "2026-10-22" RETURN s.address AS from_address, r.address AS to_address, x.tx_id AS tx_id, x.sold_asset AS sold_asset, x.bought_asset AS bought_asset, x.sold_usd AS sold_usd, x.bought_usd AS bought_usd LIMIT 25
recipes.description: The swaps of a seller and the exchange router on one day (skill chain-insights-dex-gauge, reference G4): a pair-and-day facts read that gives each swap's tx_id and its sold and bought assets, the key to the router's own transfer of that transaction. Rows depend on the day; the shape is what the lane admits.

recipes.query: USE facts MATCH (s:Address {address: "0x4b9364c8553c519a419b259f022865071fd7bfdf"})-[x:SWAP]->(m:Address {address: "0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951"}) WHERE x.block_date = "2026-10-22" RETURN s.address AS from_address, m.address AS to_address, x.recipient AS recipient, x.tx_id AS tx_id, x.sold_asset AS sold_asset, x.bought_asset AS bought_asset LIMIT 25
recipes.description: The buyer past a pool manager (skill chain-insights-dex-vault): the facts SWAP row of the seller and the Uniswap v4 PoolManager on one day carries the recipient, which is the buyer when it is not the manager itself. Never a topology hop out of the manager, which has 480,000 receivers. Rows depend on the day.
